newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dlr stays bid at close, TWI slips on hard yen.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dlr stays bid at close, TWI slips on hard yen.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index stole the limelight in New Zealand's foreign exchange market on Monday as the U.S. dollar fell sharply against the yen.

The yen's strength saw the TWI slip to 67.28 by the close from its 67.47, bringing monetary conditions well below those assumed by the central bank in March. The TWI ended around 10 points above its session lows.
The kiwi finished at US$0.6892/99, from its 0.6890/97 open and 0.6865/73 close on Friday, after being boosted in early trade by a bid Australian currency and ongoing eurokiwi issuance.
"As everyone understands, (the TWI weakness) is not the result of a loss of faith in the New Zealand dollar -- it's just the fact that dollar/yen has been moving very strongly.
"There are a lot of yen/Aussie trades going through, and again, our mechanical TWI has just been responding passively," a dealer said.
Meanwhile, short bank bill rates moved upwards but failed to cancel out the impact of the falling TWI on the MCI.

The Reuters Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) showed market conditions temporarily more than 100 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level twice during the day, before coming back to end at 96 points below the assumed level.

Although a number of money market observers told Reuters late last week they felt the RBNZ was likely to express its concern at the easing in conditions, the yen-driven TWI shift during Monday appeared beyond the bank's reach, dealers said.
"The RB is caught between a rock and a hard place," ANZ Investment Bank's Murray Hindley said.

The most likely escape route would be a rebound in the dollar/yen from the sub-112 levels seen during Monday, he added. Dealers said the expectation from Tokyo and other major centres was that the dollar would bounce back in the fairly near term.
